results.fact: Approach from Gladys Divide area to the notch
results.correct_value: Leave the Gladys Divide trail at ~4,400 ft near a small pond, climb SE to below Sawtooth Pass, traverse right under The Fin's west face to the notch south of The Horn.
results.evidence: Waypoints, itinerary day 2 and its schedule, timing sectionBreakdown and the Flapjack bivy entry all send parties off the trail at ~4,400 ft to Sawtooth Pass; the bivy entry names the Needle Pass couloir as Mount Cruiser's line. The Mountaineers route page (seen via search excerpt; direct fetch returned 403) describes scrambling right under the west face of The Fin instead of continuing to Sawtooth Pass and on to the notch south of The Horn. Beta, the approach variant, pitch_detail, turnaround, detailed_rack, climate, approach and bail were brought into line.

patches.fact: Approach from Gladys Divide area to the notch
patches.find: From Gladys Divide beyond Flapjack Lakes, the standard approach climbs a steep snow/scree gully to Needle Pass - icy and typically needing crampons and an axe into midsummer. A climbers'/goat trail then bypasses The Needle and Castle Spires along loose, exposed class 3-4 terrain to the notch south of The Horn.
patches.replace: Above Flapjack Lakes, the standard approach leaves the Gladys Divide trail at about 4,400 ft, short of the divide near a small pond, and climbs an open snow/rock slope southeast toward Sawtooth Pass - snow lingers on it into midsummer, so carry an axe early in the season. Below the pass, traverse right on loose, exposed class 3-4 ground under the west face of The Fin to the notch south of The Horn.

patches.fact: Approach from Gladys Divide area to the notch
patches.find: and up to Gladys Divide, with a reserved overnight permit for the lakes basin arranged well in advance. From the divide the tread turns primitive and you gain the crest through a steep snow-and-scree gully that commonly holds ice into midsummer, so an axe and crampons earn their weight on an early trip. A climbers' and goat path then works along the crest, circumventing the Needle and the Castle Spires on loose, exposed class 3-4 ground.
patches.replace: and on toward Gladys Divide, with a reserved overnight permit for the lakes basin arranged well in advance. Short of the divide, near a small pond at about 4,400 ft, you leave the tread for an open snow-and-rock slope climbing southeast toward Sawtooth Pass; it commonly holds snow into midsummer, so an axe earns its weight on an early trip. Below the pass, a loose, exposed class 3-4 traverse leads right under The Fin's west face.

results.fact: Approach trail named in seasonal guidance
results.correct_value: The approach is Staircase / North Fork Skokomish / Flapjack Lakes, not the Putvin Trail.

results.fact: How the wilderness permit is obtained
results.correct_value: Permits only by advance reservation (or through the Wilderness Information Center); no trailhead self-registration, no same-day walk-ups; Flapjack Lakes is a quota area limited year round.
results.evidence: NPS wilderness reservations page: no paper self-registration permits at trailheads any more, no sites held as same-day walk-ups, Flapjack Lakes is a quota area. NPS Flapjack Lakes Trail page: camping permits limited year round, peak season June 15-Sept 30. WTA's permit page lists Olympic permits only via advance reservation (Flapjack online window Jun 15-Oct 15) and mentions no Olympic self-registration.

results.fact: Distance and elevation of Flapjack Lakes from the trailhead
results.evidence: The row states the lakes at 7 mi (waypoint, itinerary, 3.4+3.6), 7.5 mi (bivy), and '~4,000 ft, 8 miles' (approach), with elevations 3,850/3,900/~4,000. NPS gives 7.5 mi to 3,900 ft; WTA gives 15.4 mi round trip (7.7 one way) and a 3,850 ft high point. The two sources do not agree on one figure, so no patch.
